anomalies.observed: On the CM4 sheet, Global_EN (Module2A pin 99, net NET0180) is not connected to any switch; it is driven by the open-drain output of buffer U18 (pin 4 = NET0180), whose input (pin 2 = NET0135) is the CM4's own nEXTST output (pin 24). U18's /OE (pin 1) is tied to GND and there is no pull-up resistor on NET0180 anywhere on the sheet.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the intended design ties GLOBAL_EN directly to a switch with no sequencing/buffer element: 'Module1 pin 99 (Global_EN) — GLOBAL_EN net, tied directly to SW1 pin 2' and 'the netlist confirms there is currently no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection.'

evidence.quote: Module1 pin 99 (Global_EN) — GLOBAL_EN net, tied directly to SW1 pin 2 ... the netlist confirms there is currently no delay/sequencing IC on this net, only a direct switch connection.
CM4 sheet: Module2A pin 99 = NET0180 (Global_EN); U18 pin 4 = NET0180; U18 pin 2 = NET0135; Module2A pin 24 = NET0135 (nEXTST); U18 pin 1 = GND; no switch or pull-up on NET0180.

anomalies.impact: The CM4 power-enable line is no longer the intended manual-switch signal. It is instead an open-drain buffer output that follows the CM4's own reset output, and with no pull-up it floats when the buffer is off, so Global_EN is not reliably driven high at power-on. This changes the enable/boot behaviour away from the documented reference design.

parsed.summary: Most of the build matches the spec's described architecture (two MCP2515 + isolated transceivers + M12 CAN connectors, LTC4412 + P-MOS ideal diode, ISL54222 analog switches, WS2812 chain, SN74LVC1G07 buffers, 16 MHz CAN crystals, CAN TVS arrays), and the designator numbers differ from the spec only as a renumbering artifact. The one functional deviation the drawing supports is the Global_EN path: the spec says it is tied directly to a switch, but the schematic routes CM4 pin 99 through an open-drain buffer driven by nEXTST with no pull-up, altering the intended enable/boot behaviour.
